title: Framework activation can produce a hollow Statement of Applicability with no error, indistinguishable from a legitimate empty state
description:
`activateFramework()` seeds `client_requirements`/`client_controls` from `FrameworkRequirement` rows. If the framework's requirement catalog was never authored (zero `isLeaf:true, status:'active'` rows), the function does NOT throw - it logs a warning and returns quietly: `vibrantix-backend/src/core/client-compliance-sync.service.js:168-176` returns `{clientRequirements:0, clientControls:0}` with only a `logger.warn`. The caller (`client-frameworks.controller.js:151-171`) only surfaces an error on a thrown exception, so this path returns 201 success with `ClientFramework.status:'active'` already committed. `FrameworksManager.jsx:421-443` then renders the tile as Active, '0 controls', and a CircularProgress at 0% - visually identical to a legitimately-activated framework that simply has no coverage yet.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor sampling a framework's Statement of Applicability cannot distinguish 'this org has done nothing yet' from 'this framework's catalog was never actually populated in the platform.' There is no '0 requirements seeded - activation may have failed' state anywhere in the frontend.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3 Statement of Applicability must identify all necessary controls
